_comment: 🛑 DO NOT APPLY THIS FILE YET. 🛑
S3 bucket policy ADDITION — agrisync-raw-ap-south-1. Encryption-header deny.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
Split out of bucket-policy.json per round-1 review finding C1 (2026-08-15) —
it was there, labelled 'Phase 1, safe to apply now'. It was not.
WHY THIS IS NOT SAFE TO APPLY TODAY, STATED PLAINLY:
s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption in a Deny/Null condition checks the REQUEST
HEADER a writer sends, not the bucket's default encryption (currently
AES256 on this bucket, confirmed live — but that is irrelevant to this
condition key). A Null-condition Deny on s3:PutObject denies every write
that omits the header, and the same Deny also covers multipart UploadPart,
which cannot carry that header at all (it is set once at
CreateMultipartUpload).
THE SHARP EDGE ON THIS BUCKET SPECIFICALLY: S3RawBlobStore.PutAsync
(src/apps/ShramSafal/ShramSafal.Infrastructure/Storage/S3RawBlobStore.cs)
swallows the exception on a failed PutObject — a caller sees no error. If
this statement is applied and for any reason a PutObject to this bucket
ever arrives without the header (a bug, a refactor, a bypass of
S3RawBlobStore by future tooling, a multipart upload for a large object),
the write is denied and NOTHING SURFACES THAT FAILURE — a farmer's app
would show success while the voice clip or receipt evidence silently never
reached durable storage. This is the exact failure class the whole
architecture migration exists to end, and it is a SEPARATE hazard from the
CMK deny rail's ordering trap (aws/raw/bucket-policy-cmk-deny-rail.
PHASE2-DO-NOT-APPLY.json) — do not conflate the two files or assume
resolving one resolves the other.
IN-REPO WRITER CHECK (partial reassurance, not proof): the one confirmed
in-repo writer, S3RawBlobStore.PutAsync, DOES set an encryption method on
every PutObjectRequest (ServerSideEncryptionMethod, AES256 or AWSKMS
depending on whether KmsKeyId is configured — see that file's PutAsync
method). But (a) the AWS SDK setting ServerSideEncryptionMethod on the
request object is not independently confirmed here to translate to the
exact x-amz-server-side-encryption wire header this condition checks
(reasonable to assume, not verified against a live PUT — this lane made
zero mutating calls), and (b) that PUT is never multipart today (the code
buffers the whole payload into a MemoryStream first, i.e. always a single
PutObjectAsync call) — but nothing in this bucket's policy prevents some
future writer from using multipart, and this Deny would silently break it.
TO MAKE THIS SAFE TO APPLY:
Verify with a real (non-mutating-agent) PUT that the header actually
lands on the wire as expected, decide whether multipart needs to be
supported on this bucket at all (if never, document that invariant
explicitly rather than relying on 'nobody does it yet'), then merge this
Statement into bucket-policy.json's Statement array (not a second
put-bucket-policy call) and apply via aws/raw/apply-config.sh as one
transaction.
